general_query_list.answer: Status meeting. AWS and the repository are set up, but the telematics vendor's new API (needed for odometer readings) slips to the second week of January, so the team agreed to move the Pune go-live from 15 January to 1 February rather than launch with manual readings. Because the back workshop bays at Pune have no signal, the team agreed the mechanics' Android app will work offline and sync later, with device-side timestamps and encrypted local storage. Operations will run an HR driver satisfaction survey at Pune in February, separate from FleetCare. Notifications for version one will be email only. Meera's idea of a reporting read replica was deferred until query load is known.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Morning everyone. Let's go straight into status. Arjun?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Mixed news. The good part: the cloud account is set up, the repo's there, and we've got the work order screens working against a test database.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: And the bad part?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: The telematics vendor. We need their API to get odometer readings from the trucks, that's what drives the service intervals. They told us on Monday their new API version won't be available until the second week of January.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: So without it the system doesn't know when trucks are due?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: It can, if someone types the odometer readings in manually, but that's exactly the spreadsheet problem again.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: And my due-date logic depends on that feed. Without it the overdue list is guesswork.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: How much would that push us?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Realistically two weeks after they deliver, to integrate and test. So end of January.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: I'd rather go live late than go live with manual readings. The mechanics will lose trust on day one.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay. I don't love it, but I agree. So we're moving the Pune go-live from the fifteenth of January to the first of February. Everyone agree?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes, first of Feb is realistic.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Agreed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Agreed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: I'll tell the leadership group. Sara, anything that changes for you?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: No, just the timing of the security review, I'll move it.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Next item. Tom, the workshop connectivity issue you raised.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Yeah. I walked around Pune with a phone. The back workshop bays, where the heavy trucks go, have basically no signal. It's a metal shed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: That's important. If the app needs a connection to mark a job done, they'll just stop using it.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: What I'd propose: the Android app works offline. It keeps the day's jobs on the phone, they can complete jobs and log parts with no signal, and it syncs when the phone gets a connection again.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: As long as the sync keeps the actual completion time, not the sync time. Otherwise my reports are wrong.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes, we'd timestamp on the device.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: The data on the phone needs to be encrypted. They're company devices with MDM, so that's manageable.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Cost to build?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Maybe a week and a half extra. It fits inside the new date.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Then we go with it. The mechanics' Android app will support offline mode and sync later.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Good. That solves the shed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Tom, you had something about a survey?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Yes, separate from FleetCare really. HR wants us to run a driver satisfaction survey, and we thought Pune first because it's the biggest depot. Probably in February.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Paper or online?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Online, a simple form, plus paper for anyone who wants it.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Do we need to coordinate it with the pilot? I don't want people confused by two new things at once.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Drivers don't use FleetCare, only mechanics do. So I think it's fine.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay. Then the driver survey runs at Pune in February, operations owns it, and it's not part of this project. Agreed?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Agreed.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Notifications. Tom, what did the depot leads say about SMS?

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Honestly, mixed. The Pune lead said most mechanics would rather get an email to their work address, they all have one and it shows on the phone anyway. Nagpur didn't answer.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Sara
meeting_transcripts.content: Email is much simpler for me. No personal numbers.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: And email costs us nothing, we already have a mail service set up.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: So for version one, notifications are email only. We can look at SMS later if people ask for it.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Fine by me.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Tom
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: One question about the data. For reporting, I wanted to put a reporting database next to the main one, maybe a separate PostgreSQL read replica.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Arjun
meeting_transcripts.content: Let's not decide that today. I want to see how heavy your queries are first.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Meera
meeting_transcripts.content: Fair, I'll send you some sample queries.

meeting_transcripts.speaker: Priya
meeting_transcripts.content: Okay, anything else? No? Thanks everyone.
